title: Localization model and Brown representation before splitting the unit
statement: Let A be an abelian category of objects in Type uA and morphisms in Type vA, Grothendieck relative to w, with a chosen w-Hom derived category D(A) and coproducts indexed by Type max(w,vA,vH). Let H : D(A)^op → AddCommGrpCat.{vH} be homological and preserve discrete limits indexed by that same universe. There exist a category B of object universe max(uA,vA,max(w,vH)+1) and Hom universe max(w,vH), functors L : B → D(A) and R : D(A) → B, an adjunction L left adjoint to R with invertible counit, and an object E of B naturally representing L.op followed by the underlying set functor of H and ULift.{w}. This assertion provides no split unit and no retract in D(A).

source.place: injectives-lemma-brown, first paragraph (using derived Gabriel-Popescu, Tag 0F5V)

proof.text: Obtain the compactly generated triangulated source B, its coproducts, and the exact localization adjunction L left adjoint to R with invertible counit from lem-g2-grothendieck-derived-compact-localization-model. Install the returned structures locally.

Set K = L.op composed with H. The opposite of a triangulated functor is triangulated, so K is homological. For each index type I in Type max(w,vH), transfer hH for ULift I in Type max(w,vA,vH) along the discrete equivalence. L is a left adjoint, hence L.op preserves limits, so K preserves the required discrete limits.

Apply the proved adopted-source brownCohomologicalRepresentabilityUniverseTransfer to B, hB, K and hK. This needs no additional common-universe Brown principle and gives a representing object E and representing-by structure.

Lift the representing-by structure through uliftFunctor and convert it to the displayed lifted-Yoneda isomorphism using Mathlib representableByUliftFunctorEquiv and RepresentableBy.equivUliftYonedaIso. Return B, L, R, adjunction, invertible counit and E.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0F5X, first paragraph; same localization and Brown argument using the stronger source universe-transfer theorem directly.
